items.title: Codimension zero points of a normalization are images of codimension zero points

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism f : Y -> X of schemes with normalization X' -> X of X in Y, every codimension zero point x' of X' is the image of a codimension zero point y of Y (source lines 10107-10115). The proof reduces to an affine base X = Spec(A) using etale locality of the normalization, so that X' = Spec(A') with A' the integral closure of A in the global sections of Y and x' corresponds to a minimal prime of A'; choosing a surjective etale V = Spec(B) -> Y with V affine, the map A' -> B is injective, so every minimal prime of A' is the image of a minimal prime of B by the algebra lemma on minimal primes.
